docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w3-kernel/* (raw disk dumps, serial logs, console screenshots, NOTES.md)

gap_a_fat16_extend_write.finding: NOT a kernel bug. mkfs.fat -C ftruncates the target to the requested size FIRST, then setup_tables() rejects sizes below FAT16's 4087-cluster floor with 'too small or a too large filesystem' — so content is never written on a 1 MiB image; only the ftruncate zero-fill persists (exactly w2's all-zeros PROBE.IMG). No kernel write-path change was needed or made.
proof_tiers: Failing-test-first: fs_test test_fs_ftruncate_extend_then_write (process/file layer, open->ftruncate(4MiB)->lseek0->write pattern->close->reopen->byte compare) PASSES.
Failing-test-first: fat16_test test_fat16_ftruncate_extend_then_write (/W3F16.IMG 4 MiB, 0x1F+(i&0x3F), watermarks {0,512,512*8,size-4096}, reopen+compare) PASSES.
Host parity: obj/mkfs_host/mkfsfat_host -F 16 -C at 1024/4096/8192 blocks dies with 'too small' BEFORE content writes; 16384 blocks (16 MiB) and 131072 (128 MiB) pass (rc=0, exact size).

In-OS 1 MiB (raw disk): mkfsfat -F 16 -C PROBE.IMG 1024 -> 'WARNING: Not attempting to create a too small or a too large filesystem'; PROBE.IMG.raw = 1,048,576 B ALL ZEROS (magic 00 00 00, no FAT16 string, no 55AA) — chain allocated by ftruncate, no content.

In-OS 16 MiB (raw disk, decisive): mkfsfat -F 16 -C OUT.IMG 16384 -> 'mkfs.fat 4.2 (2021-01-31)' banner; OUT.IMG.raw = 16,777,216 B; boot magic EB 3C 90, 'FAT16' at +54, 55 AA at +510, non-zero content, FAT chain of 1024 clusters present. Content persists byte-exact through a graceful QMP quit.
gap_a_fat16_extend_write.result: closed (re-diagnosed; kernel write path verified persistent)

gap_b_dirent.fix: src/libc/src/dirent.c rewritten to call the existing SYS_READ_DIR syscall (row 15; kernel name cap 31 chars frozen per AD-13; d_name is 256 bytes so the cap always fits). opendir() does a stat()-based is-dir check so non-directories return ENOTDIR. Previously opendir/readdir/closedir returned ENOSYS.
gap_b_dirent.kernel: Kernel read_dir was already functional; no kernel change. Added kernel coverage: fat16_test test_fat16_read_dir_multiple (/W3RDDIR with 8.3 + long-name entries + subdir + empty dir, iteration asserts >=5 entries).
gap_b_dirent.end_to_end: In-OS: staged DENTEST.BIN (real libc consumer, opendir/readdir/closedir) enumerates /FIXTURE and /FIXTURE/SUB and writes /DENTEST.OUT; extracted 33 bytes decode to ['.','..','ONE.TXT','SUB','.','..','TWO.TXT'] — full enumeration including subdirectory descent, previously impossible (ENOSYS).
gap_b_dirent.result: closed (libc dirent wired end-to-end; ENOSYS path removed)
